pr.title: FIX: proper handling of group memberships

raw_findings.body: The pager reports "1/2" instead of "1/1", `showingLast` stays false so "next" is enabled, and clicking it sets offset to user_count and renders an empty member list.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Pagination state is inconsistent with the actual number of pages, letting the user navigate past the end of the member list.
raw_findings.impact: The pager reports "1/2" instead of "1/1", `showingLast` stays false so "next" is enabled, and clicking it sets offset to user_count and renders an empty member list.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new pagination computed property adds 1 to a floored division instead of using a ceiling division, so an exactly-full last page is counted twice.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the page count as `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` instead of `Math.floor(...) + 1`.
raw_findings.title: totalPages off-by-one produces a phantom empty last page
raw_findings.trigger: Open the admin page of a group whose member count is an exact multiple of the page size (e.g. 50 members with the default limit of 50), then look at the pager / click the "next" arrow.

raw_findings.body: The server serializes an arbitrarily large number of GroupUser records in one request, causing large memory/CPU spikes and slow responses on public group pages.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unbounded caller-controlled query size on a publicly reachable endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: The server serializes an arbitrarily large number of GroupUser records in one request, causing large memory/CPU spikes and slow responses on public group pages.
raw_findings.root_cause: The rewritten `members` action moved pagination out of the automatic-group-only branch but dropped any upper bound on the caller-supplied limit.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Clamp the requested limit, e.g. `limit = [(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 200].min`, before applying it to the query.
raw_findings.title: Members endpoint accepts an unbounded `limit` parameter
raw_findings.trigger: Any client requests `/groups/<name>/members.json?limit=1000000` for a large group.

raw_findings.body: PostgreSQL rejects `OFFSET -1` and the request fails with a 500 error instead of returning the first page.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled database error surfaced as a server error for a trivially malformed query string.
raw_findings.impact: PostgreSQL rejects `OFFSET -1` and the request fails with a 500 error instead of returning the first page.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new pagination code passes the raw, unvalidated offset param directly into `offset(...)` without the lower-bound clamp that the client-side model applies.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Clamp the offset to zero, e.g. `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`, before building the query.
raw_findings.title: Negative `offset` parameter reaches SQL OFFSET and raises a 500

raw_findings.body: The `group_users` row is removed with `delete_all` semantics, so GroupUser destroy callbacks / the `user_count` counter cache never run and the group keeps reporting the old member count in the admin header and group list.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Persisted counter column drifts from the actual membership rows after every removal.
raw_findings.impact: The `group_users` row is removed with `delete_all` semantics, so GroupUser destroy callbacks / the `user_count` counter cache never run and the group keeps reporting the old member count in the admin header and group list.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new remove_member action bypasses the model's `remove` API and uses the through-association `delete`, which skips record callbacks and counter-cache maintenance.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Look up the user and call the existing `Group#remove(user)` helper (which destroys the GroupUser records) instead of `group.users.delete(user_id)`.
raw_findings.title: remove_member deletes join rows via association delete, leaving user_count stale
raw_findings.trigger: Admin clicks the remove (×) icon next to a member of a non-automatic group.

raw_findings.body: `Group#add` pushes the user onto the through association unconditionally, creating a second `group_users` row so the member appears twice in the list and `user_count` is inflated.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate membership rows are persisted for a single user.
raw_findings.impact: `Group#add` pushes the user onto the through association unconditionally, creating a second `group_users` row so the member appears twice in the list and `user_count` is inflated.
raw_findings.root_cause: The replacement of `group.usernames = ...` (which diffed additions against current members) with a plain loop of `group.add` removed the duplicate-membership guard.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Skip users already in the group, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)` (or reuse the diffing logic from `Group#usernames=`).
raw_findings.title: add_members can add an existing member twice
raw_findings.trigger: Admin types a username that is already a member of the group into the "Add members" selector and clicks Add.

raw_findings.body: `{{#if model}}` is now always truthy (model is the group, not the members array), so a header-only `<table class='group-members'>` is rendered while members load and for groups with no members.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Template guard becomes a no-op and renders an empty widget.
raw_findings.impact: `{{#if model}}` is now always truthy (model is the group, not the members array), so a header-only `<table class='group-members'>` is rendered while members load and for groups with no members.
raw_findings.root_cause: The iteration source was switched from `model` to `members` without updating the enclosing `{{#if model}}` guard, which previously tested the members array itself.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change the surrounding guard to `{{#if members}}` so the table only renders once members are loaded and non-empty.
raw_findings.title: Group members template guard no longer prevents rendering an empty table
raw_findings.trigger: Navigate to a group's members tab; the route now sets the controller model to the group object and loads members asynchronously.

validated_findings.body: The pager reports "1/2" instead of "1/1", `showingLast` stays false so "next" is enabled, and clicking it sets offset to user_count and renders an empty member list.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Pagination state is inconsistent with the actual number of pages, letting the user navigate past the end of the member list.
validated_findings.impact: The pager reports "1/2" instead of "1/1", `showingLast` stays false so "next" is enabled, and clicking it sets offset to user_count and renders an empty member list.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new pagination computed property adds 1 to a floored division instead of using a ceiling division, so an exactly-full last page is counted twice.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the page count as `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` instead of `Math.floor(...) + 1`.
validated_findings.title: totalPages off-by-one produces a phantom empty last page
validated_findings.trigger: Open the admin page of a group whose member count is an exact multiple of the page size (e.g. 50 members with the default limit of 50), then look at the pager / click the "next" arrow.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R13 shows `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` which produces an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50/50 = 1, +1 = 2 pages instead of 1). The trigger and impact are realistic and grounded in the patch.

validated_findings.body: The server serializes an arbitrarily large number of GroupUser records in one request, causing large memory/CPU spikes and slow responses on public group pages.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unbounded caller-controlled query size on a publicly reachable endpoint.
validated_findings.impact: The server serializes an arbitrarily large number of GroupUser records in one request, causing large memory/CPU spikes and slow responses on public group pages.
validated_findings.root_cause: The rewritten `members` action moved pagination out of the automatic-group-only branch but dropped any upper bound on the caller-supplied limit.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Clamp the requested limit, e.g. `limit = [(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 200].min`, before applying it to the query.
validated_findings.title: Members endpoint accepts an unbounded `limit` parameter
validated_findings.trigger: Any client requests `/groups/<name>/members.json?limit=1000000` for a large group.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R22 shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound. A client can request an arbitrarily large limit causing performance issues. The endpoint is publicly accessible via find_group which only checks visibility.

validated_findings.body: PostgreSQL rejects `OFFSET -1` and the request fails with a 500 error instead of returning the first page.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled database error surfaced as a server error for a trivially malformed query string.
validated_findings.impact: PostgreSQL rejects `OFFSET -1` and the request fails with a 500 error instead of returning the first page.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new pagination code passes the raw, unvalidated offset param directly into `offset(...)` without the lower-bound clamp that the client-side model applies.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Clamp the offset to zero, e.g. `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`, before building the query.
validated_findings.title: Negative `offset` parameter reaches SQL OFFSET and raises a 500
validated_findings.verifier_reason: PostgreSQL does not reject negative OFFSET values - it treats them as 0 or allows them depending on version. The claim that `OFFSET -1` causes a 500 error is not substantiated by PostgreSQL behavior.

validated_findings.body: The `group_users` row is removed with `delete_all` semantics, so GroupUser destroy callbacks / the `user_count` counter cache never run and the group keeps reporting the old member count in the admin header and group list.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Persisted counter column drifts from the actual membership rows after every removal.
validated_findings.impact: The `group_users` row is removed with `delete_all` semantics, so GroupUser destroy callbacks / the `user_count` counter cache never run and the group keeps reporting the old member count in the admin header and group list.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new remove_member action bypasses the model's `remove` API and uses the through-association `delete`, which skips record callbacks and counter-cache maintenance.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Look up the user and call the existing `Group#remove(user)` helper (which destroys the GroupUser records) instead of `group.users.delete(user_id)`.
validated_findings.title: remove_member deletes join rows via association delete, leaving user_count stale
validated_findings.trigger: Admin clicks the remove (×) icon next to a member of a non-automatic group.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R90 shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` which uses association delete semantics. The Group model has `has_many :group_users, dependent: :destroy` and a `remove` method at line 276-278 that properly destroys records. Using delete bypasses callbacks and counter cache updates.

validated_findings.body: `Group#add` pushes the user onto the through association unconditionally, creating a second `group_users` row so the member appears twice in the list and `user_count` is inflated.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate membership rows are persisted for a single user.
validated_findings.impact: `Group#add` pushes the user onto the through association unconditionally, creating a second `group_users` row so the member appears twice in the list and `user_count` is inflated.
validated_findings.root_cause: The replacement of `group.usernames = ...` (which diffed additions against current members) with a plain loop of `group.add` removed the duplicate-membership guard.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Skip users already in the group, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)` (or reuse the diffing logic from `Group#usernames=`).
validated_findings.title: add_members can add an existing member twice
validated_findings.trigger: Admin types a username that is already a member of the group into the "Add members" selector and clicks Add.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The Group#add method at line 272-274 uses `self.users.push(user)` which goes through the association. Rails associations with has_many :through typically handle duplicates via database constraints. Without evidence of missing unique constraint, the duplicate claim is unsubstantiated.

validated_findings.body: `{{#if model}}` is now always truthy (model is the group, not the members array), so a header-only `<table class='group-members'>` is rendered while members load and for groups with no members.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Template guard becomes a no-op and renders an empty widget.
validated_findings.impact: `{{#if model}}` is now always truthy (model is the group, not the members array), so a header-only `<table class='group-members'>` is rendered while members load and for groups with no members.
validated_findings.root_cause: The iteration source was switched from `model` to `members` without updating the enclosing `{{#if model}}` guard, which previously tested the members array itself.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Change the surrounding guard to `{{#if members}}` so the table only renders once members are loaded and non-empty.
validated_findings.title: Group members template guard no longer prevents rendering an empty table
validated_findings.trigger: Navigate to a group's members tab; the route now sets the controller model to the group object and loads members asynchronously.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The template shows `{{#if model}}` guards the table, and `{{#each m in members}}` iterates. The model is the group object which is truthy, but this renders an empty table body when members is empty - this is expected behavior for showing a table structure, not a bug.
